answer: Each agent must lock a refundable bond before it can submit work, and the bond grows with the number of identities tied to the same payment source. A randomly selected peer checks each claim; proven fraud burns the bond and pays the checker. This makes a cheap swarm of fresh accounts costly: the attacker must immobilize real capital and risks losing it for every caught lie. A public signal records the outcomes, while a private whisper cannot erase them; even saffron-colored profiles face the same rule.
